title: Agentlas Brief
description: One form, written from either side. side=offer is a package describing the method it carries; side=need is a requester describing the job. Matching compares the two directly, so a field that cannot be written from both sides may be displayed but never matched on. Sentences stay sentences: no field here is tokenised, because shredding anti-trigger sentences into the bare words 'tests' and 'ci' is what pushed a correct agent from rank 2 to rank 24 on a query that was literally its own job.

side.description: offer = a package's resume. need = a requester's work order.

locale.description: Languages this brief is written in. Kept so a sentence index never has to guess.

statement.description: offer: what this method does, in the author's own sentence. need: the user's request, verbatim. Stored and indexed as a sentence. Never split into terms for matching.

label.description: What the author or requester calls the result, in their own words. Free text forever - every domain noun in the catalogue lives here. Ranked, never filtered. The bound is deliberately loose: a first pass capped this at 200 and eight live packages failed instantly because they describe a deliverable in a full sentence ('Environment block, ranked statements with total and mean time, per-query index candidates...'), which is more useful than a noun, not less. A cap on a descriptive field is a guess about how other people write.

effect.description: What happens in the requester's world. Derived from approval requirements on the offer side; read from the request on the need side. 'other' ranks at zero and never removes a candidate.

shape.description: Computed from the OUTPUT SCHEMA'S TOPOLOGY, never authored. An array of uniform records with a per-row judgement is a ledger; a single judgement with reasons is a verdict, and so on. 38% of live output schemas already land on 'other', so the escape is load-bearing, not decorative.

format.description: md, json, csv, pptx, hwpx, diff, ... Open list. A format nobody anticipated is still a format.

contract.description: Package-relative path to the JSON Schema this deliverable validates against.

rowVerdict.description: JSON Pointer to the per-row judgement property, when the shape has one.

verdictValues.description: Copied verbatim from the publisher's own schema enum. This is NOT a controlled vocabulary - there is nothing to match it against, and no value is ever rejected.

example.description: Path to one real output instance.

exampleValid.description: Did `example` validate against `contract` at build time? null = not run. Graded by a JSON Schema validator, never by a model.

contains.description: What is actually inside the deliverable, as sentences: the output schema's property names and their descriptions. This is where a contract earns its place in matching. `label` alone is the schema title, which is usually just the package's own name again — measured: a request for a 'contract alignment log with a provision-level verdict' scored the correct DORA package 4th, because the phrase it was looking for is a PROPERTY inside that schema and the title said only 'DORA Compliance Control Room — output'. Extracted, never authored; ranked, never filtered.

about.description: One sentence naming the fact that must exist. Free text, never normalised.

stage.description: WHEN the fact comes to exist: knowable from the first sentence / answerable if asked / only inside a handed-over file / only after doing the work. This is a time axis, not a classification, so it has no escape member by design - there is no fifth moment. When undecidable the compiler must write 'intake', which becomes a question and never excludes. Only 'request' participates in unmet, and unmet is a deduction plus a printed list.

form.description: What the requester physically hands over. Scores ZERO. It exists only to print a useful note ('this method wants a repo path and you have a PDF').

pointer.description: JSON Pointer from this prose obligation into the machine intake schema property that carries it.

fallback.description: The DEGRADATION policy when the fact is absent - what the method still does, and at what reduced confidence. Not a substitute tool.

performs.description: Derived, not authored: the effect set this method actually reaches. An offer that declares nothing here can NEVER be excluded.

gated.description: Acts performed only after the host shows an approval prompt. Observed by the host runtime, which is why a model cannot claim it paused when it did not.

refuses.description: Categorical refusals, as sentences. Replaces anti_triggers, of which 29-37% were not refusals at all but neighbour routing ('that is X's job') - and it was tokenising those that cost a correct agent 22 rank positions. A neighbour's name cannot be expressed in this shape.

forbid.description: NEED SIDE ONLY, and the ONLY field in this whole form that can remove a candidate. Fires only against an offer's positively declared `performs`, and only when performs is a subset of forbid - i.e. everything the method does is forbidden. 'other' is deliberately not a member, so a publisher who fell through to 'other' is structurally unexcludable. This is the requester's own choice, not a vocabulary miss.

capability.description: A vendor-free verb phrase for what the MACHINE must be able to do: 'open the page in a real browser and read what a user would see'. Never a product.

preferred.description: The one place a product name may live (playwright, astryx, notion, slack). DISPLAY ONLY - it must never reach a matching input. Roughly 99.9% of machines have no MCP servers installed, so a package wired to its author's own tools has to remain usable by everyone else.

withoutIt.description: Required sibling of `preferred`. What this method does on a machine that lacks the facility. A requirement with no stated degradation is how a package becomes unusable to the 99.9%.

host.description: Preconditions of the METHOD on the machine, not capabilities of the agent. The runtime reads the web; the package does not. Ranked, never filtered. `permission` was removed: the owner's ruling is that permissions are not a qualification — an employer hands you a computer after hiring you, so what a host is willing to grant says nothing about whether this method fits the work.

provenance.description: Per-field record of where the value came from, keyed by JSON Pointer. 'absent' is a legal value scoring zero - an unstated capability is never inferred from adjacent prose. This is what keeps a generated brief honest about which half of it was actually read off the package.
